items.title: Why did Lionel Messi not attend the 2026 Ballon d’Or gala today?
items.description:
Lionel Messi earned his 17th career nomination after being named to the 30-man shortlist for the 2026 Ballon d'Or, but significant doubt surrounds why the eight-time winner did not attend the ceremony at the London Palladium. 
Today, the soccer world will find out who takes home the sport’s ultimate individual honor as the 2026 Ballon d’Or winner is revealed in London. Beyond the fierce debate over who will lift the golden trophy, the burning question on everyone’s mind was why eight-time winner Lionel Messi did not attend the ceremony.



Messi was not present at the London Palladium. While initial rumors suggested he might attend to present one of the evening’s major honors, his presence was ruled out before the event, as the grueling transatlantic flight from Miami to London made an in-person appearance today impossible.



“Lionel Messi will not be presenting a trophy to any of the winners at the Ballon d’Or, as he has not been invited to do so,” the soccer insider wrote on X about Messi’s possible attendance.



Is Lionel Messi nominated for the 2026 Ballon d’Or?



Yes, Lionel Messi features on the 30-man shortlist for the 2026 Ballon d’Or—a stark contrast to longtime rival Cristiano Ronaldo, who was omitted from the nominations after voters concluded his calendar year was not strong enough to warrant a spot among the finalists.



Lionel Messi of Inter Miami.



The shortlist features the game’s brightest modern stars. While Kylian Mbappé of Real Madrid and Lamine Yamal of FC Barcelona stand as the definitive frontrunners following their decisive domestic and international campaigns, Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane and other continental standouts have also garnered strong support among the voting panel.


        


Lionel Messi – Argentina | Inter MiamiKylian Mbappé – France | Real MadridLamine Yamal – Spain | FC BarcelonaHarry Kane – England | Bayern MunichJude Bellingham – England | Real MadridRodri – Spain | FC BarcelonaErling Haaland – Norway | Manchester CityVinícius Júnior – Brazil | Real MadridLautaro Martínez – Argentina | Inter MilanMichael Olise – France | Bayern MunichVitinha – Portugal | Paris Saint-GermainWilliam Saliba – France | ArsenalDeclan Rice – England | ArsenalOusmane Dembélé – France | Paris Saint-GermainPau Cubarsí – Spain | FC BarcelonaBruno Fernandes – Portugal | Manchester UnitedLuis Díaz – Colombia | LiverpoolAchraf Hakimi – Morocco | Paris Saint-GermainGabriel Magalhães – Brazil | ArsenalKhvicha Kvaratskhelia – Georgia | Paris Saint-GermainFabián Ruiz – Spain | Paris Saint-GermainMarc Cucurella – Spain | Real MadridMarquinhos – Brazil | Paris Saint-GermainJoão Neves – Portugal | Paris Saint-GermainDayot Upamecano – France | Bayern MunichFerran Torres – Spain | Paris Saint-GermainNuno Mendes – Portugal | Paris Saint-GermainWillian Pacho – Ecuador | Paris Saint-GermainSadio Mané – Senegal | Al-NassrJulián Quiñones – Mexico | Al-Qadsiah



What would happen if Lionel Messi wins the 2026 Ballon d’Or?



If Messi were to claim the 2026 Ballon d’Or in absentia, protocol dictates that the trophy would likely be accepted on his behalf by an event host or club representative, followed by a pre-recorded video acceptance speech thanking the global panel of journalists for their votes.



Lifting the award would mark an unprecedented ninth Ballon d’Or in Messi’s legendary career, adding to his historic triumphs in 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2015, 2019, 2021, and most recently in 2023 following Argentina’s 2022 FIFA World Cup victory in Qatar.

items.title: Harry Kane wins first Ballon d’Or at 33: How old were Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo when they won theirs?
items.description:
Harry Kane has secured his first Ballon d'Or at 33 after capturing the 2026 edition, but how does his age compare to that of Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo when they first won the award? 
Harry Kane claimed his maiden Ballon d’Or at 33 years and 90 days old on Monday night, making him roughly a full decade older than both Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo were when they captured their first golden balls.



The English marksman defied the odds to edge out generational stars Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe, who had entered the London Palladium as the prohibitive frontrunners following Sunday’s dramatic El Clasico. Kane’s triumph serves as the ultimate crowning achievement for a player whose relentless individual brilliance finally converged with world soccer’s top individual prize.



In sharp contrast to Kane’s veteran coronation, the icons of the preceding generation conquered the summit in their early twenties. Messi captured his first Ballon d’Or in 2009 at just 22 years old, while Ronaldo first hoisted the golden sphere in 2008 at 23 following Manchester United’s Champions League triumph.



Is Harry Kane the oldest player to win the Ballon d’Or?



While Kane’s victory at 33 represents a remarkable showcase of longevity, he is far from the oldest recipient in the competition’s history. That distinction belongs to inaugural winner Sir Stanley Matthews, who claimed the very first Ballon d’Or presented by France Football in 1956 at an astonishing 41 years and 10 months old.



Harry Kane of England.



In fact, Kane does not crack the top three oldest winners overall. Matthews comfortably leads the all-time ranking, followed by Lionel Messi, who secured his eighth trophy in 2023 at 36 years old, and Karim Benzema, who earned his coronation in 2022 at 34 years and 10 months.


        


Anchored by an astonishing 73-goal campaign across all competitions for Bayern Munich and England, Kane presented an indisputable case to global voters. His victory also ends a quarter-century drought for his home country, making him the first English player to lift the Ballon d’Or since Michael Owen in 2001.



A double triumph at the 2026 Ballon d’Or gala



The Ballon d’Or was not the only piece of silverware Kane carried away from the London Palladium. Prior to lifting the evening’s top honor, the Bayern striker took the stage to receive the Gerd Muller Trophy as the season’s top male striker, rewarded for his lethal 73-goal tally across domestic and continental fixtures.



While Kane swept both top honors on the men’s side, Mexican veteran forward Charlyn Corral claimed the women’s top striker award following an electric scoring run of her own. However, Corral could not complete an identical sweep, as the 2026 Ballon d’Or Féminin was awarded to Spanish midfield star Alexia Putellas, who secured the women’s golden ball for the third time in her legendary career.

items.title: No se atreven
items.description: El Balón de Oro tiene una imagen mucho más potente que su contenido. La elección de Kane como mejor jugador del mundo esta temporada no se asocia a la realidad. Da la sensación de componenda, de premiar en Londres a un jugador inglés, de no atreverse con Lamine y seguir dándole sólo el premio al más joven. Ya van tres. Los premios pierden prestigio con estas decisiones. El jugador del FC Barcelona, campeón del mundo, debía ser el ganador. Y no lo fue. Eligieron a un jugador que solo conoce los títulos desde que aterrizó en el Bayern, porque antes en el Tottenham no fue capaz de hacerlos campeonar. No jugó la final del Mundial ni la de la Champions y la Bundesliga está en el puesto entre tercero y cuarto de las cinco grandes ligas europeas. Es un gran jugador, sí. Un excelente goleador y un buen tipo, también. Participa más allá de solo empujar la pelota, sí. Pero la magia la tiene Lamine. Lo imprevisible, lo espectacular, lo diferente no siempre se traduce en goles, que es lo que ha llevado a Kane a repetir el título de Bota de Oro con el de Balón. Ni Champions ni Mundial pero sí el premio individual más importante hasta ahora. Pero lo distinto es Lamine. Y lo impresionante es Messi. Pero en el Balón de Oro no se atreven a casi nada.

Pero lejos del verde, Harry Kane responde bastante poco al prototipo de superestrella mundial. items.title: Alexia iguala a Aitana como triple Balón de Oro
items.description: Alexia Putellas vuelve a ser la mejor jugadora del mundo tras conquistar su tercer Balón de Oro, un reconocimiento que confirma su regreso a la cima del fútbol femenino mundial. La exfutbolista del FC Barcelona y actual capitana del London City se vistió de gala en Londres, su nueva ciudad, para levantar el trofeo ante la atenta mirada de su nueva jefa, Michele Kang, propietaria del club londinense.

items.title: El palmarés del Balón de Oro femenino con el tercero de Alexia Putellas
items.description: Alexia Putellas toma el testigo de Aitana Bonmatí, y lo hace por todo lo alto, tras conquistar el Balón de Oro en la gala celebrada este lunes en la ciudad de Londres, en una noche muy esperada por el mundo del fútbol y por los aficionados de todo el planeta. La del presente año es la octava edición en la que se entrega el galardón en su categoría femenina, un premio que, pese a su relativamente corta historia, ya cuenta con un palmarés muy significativo. Desde que lo ganó Ada Hegerberg en 2018 por primera vez, inaugurando así la lista de campeonas, son apenas cuatro las mujeres que se lo han llevado a casa, lo que da una idea de lo exclusivo que resulta este reconocimiento.

items.description: Ousmane Dembélé est un footballeur international français né à Vernon en 1997. Jeune surdoué formé en Normandie et au stade rennais, il explose à Dortmund avant de rejoindre le FC Barcelone pour pallier le départ de Neymar au PSG, c'est à l'époque le deuxième plus gros transfert de l'histoire du football. L'adaptation, gênée par les blessure, n'est pas simple pour l'ailier français, qui parvient tout de même à se faire une place en équipe de France dans le groupe qui devient champion du monde en 2018. Absent en 2020, il est de nouveau de la partie en 2022 et fait partie du 11 titulaire.

items.title: 2-3: El Andorra se estrella contra el muro del Burgos
items.description: El Andorra sigue sin encontrar la regularidad en casa. Los de Carles Manso cayeron este lunes ante el Burgos (2-3) en un encuentro trepidante que dejó cinco goles antes del descanso y una segunda mitad de dominio tricolor sin recompensa. Karrikaburu, Luengo y Curro, de penalti, castigaron los errores defensivos locales, mientras que Lautaro y Jordi Cano mantuvieron vivo al conjunto del Principado. Tras el paso por vestuarios, el Andorra encerró al Burgos en su campo y dispuso de varias ocasiones para igualar el marcador, pero se encontró con un Cantero providencial. Cuarta derrota en seis partidos en Encamp y una asignatura pendiente cada vez más evidente.

items.title: Unai Simón, ganador del premio a Mejor Portero
items.description: En una noche en la que había muchas dudas respecto a quién iba a ser el ganador del Balón de Oro, la identidad del premio a mejor portero del año, el Trofeo Lev Yashin, tenía dueño prácticamente desde que se terminó la temporada: Unai Simón Mendibil. "Muchas gracias a todos. Es un orgullo para mí estar aquí. Sería imposible sin la ayuda de muchas personas. Le doy las gracias a mis padres, a mi novia y a toda mi cuadrilla de la infancia. Ellos son los que me hacen entender que muchos de los que estamos en esta sala somos unos privilegiados. También a mis entrenadores y a todos mis compañeros de la selección y del Athletic. Me gustaría darle las gracias al Koldo Asua, que en paz descanse, que decía que el fútbol más allá de los títulos lo importante es el legado cuando esto acabe. He aprendido a amar a un club el Athletic Club, un club que me lo ha dado todo. Por todos ellos estoy recibiendo este premio aquí", dijo en primera instancia.

items.title: El palmarés del Mejor Joven Talento, copado por el Barça masculino y femenino
items.description: Raymond Kopaszewski, más conocido como Raymond Kopa, internacional francés hijo de inmigrantes polacos, mítico delantero del Angers, Stade Reims en dos etapas y Real Madrid, dio el nombre al Trofeo Kopa al Mejor Sub-21 en la Gala del Balón de Oro tanto en categoría masculina y femenina. Se instauró en 2018 y es el reconocimiento de la organización al primer francés en ganar el Balón de Oro, fallecido un año antes, en 2017. En esta edición de 2026 el premio se queda sin 'apellido' y pasa a llamarse Mejor Joven Talento.

items.title: "Se pueden alcanzar las mayores cotas defendiendo los colores del Athletic"
items.description: Jon Uriarte y Mikel González han acompañado a Unai Simón a la Gala del Balón de Oro que se celebra en Londres. El portero de Murgia es el favorito para ganar el Trofeo Yashin. "Es una noticia buenísima, muy difícil de conseguir. Unai entró muy joven en nuestra cantera, ha ido dando pasos, desarrollándose como jugador y como persona. Que haya llegado hasta aquí y pueda aspirar a ganar el premio a mejor portero del mundo es algo increíble. Es algo muy positivo, principalmente para él porque nadie le ha regalado nada, y también para todos los entrenadores que ha tenido. items.description: Llega una de las semanas más esperadas en mucho tiempo para el Barça de fútbol sala: el regreso a la Champions League. Los culés se medirán al equipo anfitrión, al Futsal Minerva suizo y al FC Semey kazajo en busca de un billete hacia los octavos de final. Se clasifican los tres primeros, por lo que el Barça no debería tener problemas para avanzar en la próxima fase de la Champions.

items.description: Gli Azzurri show positive signs of improvement in seesaw 3-3 draw against a Roma side inspired by Messi-like Matías SouléScott McTominay was leaving nothing to doubt. He appeared to have scored with a close-range header early in the second half of Napoli’s game at home to Roma, but Pierluigi Gollini clawed the ball out from inside the goal. McTominay got his noggin to the rebound, nudging it back across the line. Roma’s keeper pushed away again, so the Napoli midfielder got to his feet and smashed the loose ball into the back of the net.Just typical. You wait two months for your first goal of the Serie A season, then three show up at once. They only counted for one, of course, but McTominay looked happy enough with that as he ran to thank Matteo Politano for the assist. Continue reading...

items.title: Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho downplays defeating Barcelona: ‘We must not go over the moon’
items.description:
Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho moved quickly to temper euphoria following his side's dramatic 2–1 victory over FC Barcelona at Spotify Camp Nou, warning his players that winning El Clasico means little unless it translates into silverware at the end of the season. 
Real Madrid secured a crucial victory against Barcelona on Matchday 10 of the 2026–27 La Liga season. However, manager Jose Mourinho firmly believes the squad must avoid complacency, reminding them that the job is far from finished and the domestic campaign remains long and grueling.



Propelled by a clinical brace from Kylian Mbappe—who reached the historic milestone of 100 goals in a Real Madrid shirt—Los Blancos marched into Spotify Camp Nou and walked away with three vital points in hand. Nevertheless, Madrid remain third in the La Liga standings, and Mourinho is acutely aware that his players must keep their feet firmly planted on the ground if they hope to lift silverware at the end of the season.



“In my view, Real Madrid do not play to win at the Camp Nou… Real Madrid play to win LaLiga,” Mourinho said after the game. “This must be the mentality. We need to continue like this and don’t go over the moon after this win.”



Real Madrid locked in a vital win on Matchday 10



Entering Sunday’s showdown, Real Madrid trailed the Blaugrana by six points in the table. This away triumph allowed them to slash the deficit to just three points, keeping alive their ambitions of overtaking both Barcelona and second-place Atletico Madrid to claim the top spot before the mid-season winter break.



Jose Mourinho of Real Madrid



Achieving this victory without the suspended Vinicius Junior and starting goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois—who was sidelined on Sunday morning with a severe flu—showcased the squad’s tactical maturity and proved they do not rely solely on individual star names. With a healthier, deeper bench, Real Madrid are once again being viewed as genuine contenders both domestically and in the UEFA Champions League, where they maintain a strong European campaign.


        


Last season, recurring injuries severely undermined Real Madrid’s consistency and depth, limiting their ability to challenge on all fronts. If Mourinho can keep his core squad fit and firing over the grueling winter schedule, this Madrid team possesses every ingredient required to restore the dominant standard expected at the Santiago Bernabeu.

items.title: Kylian Mbappe hits 100 goals with Real Madrid in win over Barcelona, falls short of Cristiano Ronaldo’s historic pace
items.description:
Kylian Mbappe delivered a masterclass at Spotify Camp Nou, scoring both goals in Real Madrid's 2–1 victory over FC Barcelona to reach a historic milestone of 100 goals for Los Blancos. 
Kylian Mbappe enjoyed a banner night in Catalonia. Not only did he score the brace that powered Real Madrid to a 2–1 victory over Barcelona, but he also reached the century mark for Los Blancos—even if it fell just shy of Cristiano Ronaldo’s record-setting pace.



Mbappe has been an indispensable asset for Real Madrid since arriving in the summer of 2024. His match-winning display at Spotify Camp Nou took him to 100 goals in just 115 competitive appearances. While a remarkable feat of elite consistency, it leaves him just behind the benchmark set by his childhood idol.



Ronaldo reached his first century of goals for Real Madrid in an astonishing 105 matches. The Portuguese icon achieved the milestone in 10 fewer games than Mbappe, cementing his position alongside legendary forward Ferenc Puskás among the most lethal finishers in club history.



It couldn’t arrive at a better time



While Mbappe’s hyper-competitive drive might have craved breaking Ronaldo’s record outright, the milestone could not have arrived at a more opportune moment. Delivering it against Madrid’s fiercest rivals on hostile territory added poetic justice to a victory that trimmed Barcelona’s lead at the top of La Liga from six points to just three.







Mbappe’s relentless hunger was on full display throughout the contest. By reaching this landmark while deciding El Clasico, the Frenchman provided the exact psychological catalyst Real Madrid required to re-establish their domestic title credentials and signal that the championship race is wide open.


        


Real Madrid now sit third in the table, having leapfrogged Real Betis and closed in on both second-place Atletico Madrid and leaders Barcelona. Armed with consecutive statement victories across La Liga and the Champions League, Los Blancos head toward the winter break looking every bit like genuine frontrunners on both fronts.

items.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
items.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written.“The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

items.title: Udinese vs AC Milan: Projected lineups for the 2026-27 Serie A match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Udinese vs AC Milan in the 2026-27 Serie A. Udinese host AC Milan in a matchup pairing a team in freefall against a side that has found its scoring touch.
Udinese come into this one on a three-game losing skid, falling 0-3 to Lecce on October 18 after a 1-2 defeat to Torino the week before. Before that stretch they were beaten 0-1 by Cagliari on September 19, leaving them without a win across their last three outings. Three points here would do plenty to stop the bleeding and settle nerves around Kosta Runjaic’s group.
AC Milan arrive in better shape, having beaten Atalanta 3-2 on October 18 after a 1-1 draw with Sassuolo on October 11. Those results followed a 3-0 win over Lecce back on September 20, giving Milan two wins and a draw in their last three. A positive result in Udine would keep Milan’s momentum going as they push for points in the standings.
Udinese projected lineup
Runjaic sets Udinese up in a 3-4-2-1, with Maduka Okoye behind a back three of Matteo Palma, Nicolo Bertola and Enzo Ebosse. Jurgen Ekkelenkamp and Mergim Vojvoda provide the width as wingbacks, while Jesper Karlstrom and Jakub Piotrowski anchor the midfield. Giorgi Chakvetadze and Hassane Kamara sit just behind lone striker Keinan Davis, and with no absences listed, Runjaic has his full group available to try to end the losing run.
Udinese projected starting XI (3-4-2-1): Maduka Okoye, James Abankwah, Christian Kabasele, Matteo Palma, Giorgi Chakvetadze, Mergim Vojvoda, Jakub Piotrowski, Jesper Karlstrom, Jurgen Ekkelenkamp, Hassane Kamara, Keinan Davis. Coach: Kosta Runjaic.
AC Milan projected lineup
Ruben Amorim mirrors the setup with a 3-4-2-1 for AC Milan, starting Mike Maignan in goal behind Fikayo Tomori, Koni De Winter and Strahinja Pavlovic. Filippo Terracciano and Alphadjo Cisse operate as wingbacks, with Yunus Musah and Luka Modric controlling the center of the park. Christian Pulisic and Pervis Estupinan are tasked with supporting Goncalo Ramos up top, and Milan have no absences to work around as they look to build on their recent form.
AC Milan projected starting XI (3-4-2-1): Mike Maignan, Fikayo Tomori, Koni De Winter, Strahinja Pavlovic, Filippo Terracciano, Alphadjo Cisse, Yunus Musah, Luka Modric, Christian Pulisic, Pervis Estupinan, Goncalo Ramos. Coach: Ruben Amorim.

items.title: Is Raphinha playing today? Confirmed lineups for Barcelona vs Real Madrid in 2026-27 LaLiga Matchday 10
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Barcelona vs Real Madrid in the 2026-27 LaLiga and if Raphinha is playing today for the Blaugranas. Barcelona and Real Madrid meet in the 2026-27 LaLiga. Here are the projected lineups, with Raphinha expected to play today as starter after recovering from his injury.
Barcelona come in off a win against Betis (5-2). Before that, they beat Getafe 3-0. They arrive on a winning run and will try to extend it here.
In their most recent outing, Real Madrid beat Sevilla 4-1. That followed a win against Villarreal (1-0). They have won 2 of their last 3 and want more of the same here.
Barcelona confirmed lineup
Barcelona line up in a 4-2-3-1. Andreas Christensen is unavailable. The Blaugranas seek a key victory at home to secure a nine point lead over Real Madrid.
Barcelona confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Joan García, Xavi Espart Font, Pau Cubarsí, Gerard Martín, João Cancelo, Rodri, Fermín López, Pedri, Lamine Yamal, Raphinha, Anthony Gordon. Coach: Hansi Flick.
Real Madrid confirmed lineup
Real Madrid line up in a 4-2-3-1. Ferland Mendy is unavailable. Los Blancos seek a tough win on the road in order to not let Barcelona and Atletico Madrid get too separated from them in the standings and maintain the title hope very much alive.
Real Madrid confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Andriy Lunin, Federico Valverde, Ibrahima Konaté, Dean Huijsen, Marc Cucurella, Bernardo Silva, Jude Bellingham, Aurélien Tchouaméni, Arda Güler, Kylian Mbappé, Yan Diomande. Coach: José Mourinho.

items.title: Fernandes gamble leaves Carrick to carry the can for United’s institutional failures | Will Unwin
items.description: Leaving out his captain was doomed to fail but so are the club under the current leadership and the fans at Old Trafford know that all too wellDropping your captain, who has held the team together for most of the past five years, is a bold move from a man whose job is on the line. It was very much a make-or-break decision from Michael Carrick to leave out Bruno Fernandes against Bournemouth. It did not work and Carrick knew the consequences if it failed and will probably pay the price for it, but he should not be alone.Carrick said the decision to drop the Portuguese playmaker was purely based on football reasons but criticising his manager after the desperate defeat to Como cannot have helped. Clearly Carrick disagreed with his captain’s comments on the lack of pressing in the Champions League fixture. items.title: Isak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an end
items.description: Brighton’s impressive run was blown off course at Anfield where Liverpool performed with an appetite and urgency at both ends of the pitch that showed Andoni Iraola’s methods taking root. It was Liverpool, deserving winners on home soil for the first time in the Premier League this season, who looked upwardly mobile.There was more evidence of the expensive trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola feeling at home and adapting to Iraola’s demands. Wirtz was instrumental in an opening goal officially credited to Brighton’s Pascal Gross and Isak scored for the sixth time in six Premier League appearances to shatter the visitors’ sequence of four successive league wins. The sight of Barcola sprinting back to help his defence and Ronald Araújo smashing into challenges, as Liverpool stubbornly defended their lead and their box in the second half, satisfied Iraola just as much as his side’s incisiveness before the break. items.title: Manchester United vs Bournemouth: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Premier League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Manchester United vs Bournemouth in the 2026-27 Premier League. Manchester United and Bournemouth meet in the 2026-27 Premier League. Here are the projected lineups.
Manchester United come in off a draw against Leeds (1-1). Before that, they drew with Tottenham 1-1. They are still looking for a win in their last 3 games.
In their most recent outing, Bournemouth beat Sunderland 2-0. That followed a loss against Chelsea (1-5). They have won 1 of their last 3 and want more of the same here.
Manchester United confirmed lineup
Manchester United line up in a 4-2-3-1. Tom Heaton is unavailable.
Manchester United confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Senne Lammens, Leny Yoro, Ayden Heaven, Harry Maguire, Diogo Dalot, Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba, Amad Diallo, Bryan Mbeumo, Mason Mount. Coach: Michael Carrick.
Bournemouth confirmed lineup
Bournemouth line up in a 4-2-3-1. Alex Tóth is unavailable.
Bournemouth confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Djordje Petrovic, Adam Smith, James Hill, Antonio Silva, Adrien Truffert, Tyler Adams, Justin Kluivert, Lewis Cook, Rayan, Evanilson, Marcus Tavernier. Coach: Marco Rose.

items.title: Liverpool vs Albion: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Premier League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Liverpool vs Albion in the 2026-27 Premier League. Liverpool host Albion at Anfield with the two sides trending in opposite directions over the last month.
Liverpool split their last three games, beating Brentford 2-1 on October 17 after a 0-3 loss to Man City on October 11, with a 1-0 win over Bournemouth back on September 20 in between. The Brentford result snapped the skid caused by the City defeat, but the manner of that loss still lingers. A win here would give Iraola’s side consecutive victories for the first time in this stretch and steady their position in the table.
Albion arrive off three straight wins, the latest a 5-0 rout of Crystal Palace on October 18 that followed a 2-0 win over Sunderland on October 10 and a 3-0 win over Arsenal on September 19. That run has them scoring freely against opponents of every level, top flight contenders included. Another result on the road would stretch the streak to four and send a message that Hürzeler’s team belong among the league’s in-form sides.
Liverpool confirmed lineup
Iraola sets Liverpool up in a 4-2-3-1 with Alisson behind a back line of Araujo, Van Dijk, Jacquet and Kerkez. Gravenberch and Mac Allister sit in midfield behind a front line of Wirtz, Barcola and Gakpo supporting Isak as the lone striker. The team is missing Frimpong, Szoboszlai, Leoni, Nallo and Ekitiké, with Ekitiké’s absence up front leaving Isak as the central reference point and shifting more creative responsibility onto Wirtz and Mac Allister.
Liverpool confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Alisson Becker, Ronald Araujo, Miloš Kerkez, Alexis Mac Allister, Jérémy Jacquet, Virgil van Dijk, Cody Gakpo, Ryan Gravenberch, Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola. Coach: Andoni Iraola.
Albion confirmed lineup
Hürzeler goes with a mirrored 4-2-3-1, Verbruggen in goal protected by Kadioglu, Vušković, Dunk and Boscagli. Gross and Ayari anchor midfield, with Andrés and Gómez tucked behind Kostoulas and De Cuyper in the front four. Albion are without Struijk, Wieffer, Tzimas, Minteh, Ferguson, Yohanna, Azeez and Mitoma, a long absentee list that puts extra weight on Kostoulas to lead the attack and on Gross and Ayari to control the tempo without their usual depth options.
Albion confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Bart Verbruggen, Ferdi Kadioglu, Olivier Boscagli, Chema Andrés, Luka Vušković, Lewis Dunk, Diego Gómez, Pascal Groß, Charalampos Kostoulas, Yasin Ayari, Maxim De Cuyper. Coach: Fabian Hürzeler.

Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.”To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. items.title: Why is Lionel Messi not starting for Inter Miami vs New York Red Bulls in 2026 MLS?
items.description:
Lionel Messi starts on the bench for Inter Miami against Red Bull New York after traveling back from Spain, with the team already through to the MLS playoffs. 
Lionel Messi is not in Inter Miami’s starting lineup for the match against Red Bull New York, as head coach Cristian “Kily” Gonzalez opted to leave the Argentine star on the bench. Messi is not injured, and the decision comes just hours after his return from Spain.



Gonzalez’s choice appears to be about rest. Messi traveled to Oviedo to receive the Princess of Asturias Award for Sports on Oct. 23 and flew back to the United States right after the ceremony, leaving him little time to recover or train with the team before the match at Sports Illustrated Stadium.



The context of the match also made the decision easier for Gonzalez. Inter Miami have already clinched a spot in the MLS Cup Playoffs, and Nashville SC have already secured the Supporters’ Shield, which leaves Miami with no chance of competing for it. The team’s priority now is to finish second in the Eastern Conference and prepare for the postseason as defending MLS Cup champions.



Messi is still available to play and is expected to get minutes off the bench in the second half, although there is a chance he may not play at all. “We should feel proud that he, through his own initiative, wants to be with us and wants to play,” Gonzalez said of the captain, who scored twice in Miami’s previous match, a 3-1 win over Atlanta United.




Here's how we line up. 📋 pic.twitter.com/jmnh20Lfk3— Inter Miami CF (@InterMiamiCF) October 24, 2026




Inter Miami and Red Bull New York confirmed lineups



In Messi’s absence, Fillipi Riquelme gets the nod in the attack and Luis Suarez will wear the captain’s armband, with German Berterame completing the front line. 


        


Inter Miami arrive in search of a fourth straight win and second in the Eastern Conference with 56 points, while Red Bull New York, managed by Michael Bradley, are 10th in the league table with 36.



Inter Miami (4-3-3): Dayne St. Clair; Gonzalo Lujan, Casemiro, Micael, Sergio Reguilon; Rodrigo De Paul, David Ayala, Matias Galarza; Fillipi Riquelme, Luis Suarez (C), German Berterame.



Red Bull New York (4-3-3): Ethan Horvath; Dylan Nealis (C), Julian Bazan, Tim Parker, Devin Padelford; Mohammed Sofo, Adri Mehmeti, Ronald Donkor; Cade Cowell, Julian Hall, Jorge Ruvalcaba.

items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Red Bulls vs Inter Miami in the 2026 MLS season. New Jersey hosts a heavyweight visitor this week as the Red Bulls welcome Inter Miami to Red Bull Arena for a matchup between two sides heading in very different directions.
The Red Bulls have dropped back to back games, falling 0-2 to Toronto FC last Saturday and 1-2 to DC on October 14. Before that stretch they looked sharp, putting four past San Diego FC in a 4-1 win on October 10. A result against Inter Miami would steady a team that has lost its last two outings and needs to arrest the slide.
Inter Miami arrive in the form of their lives, having won three straight games. They beat Atlanta United 3-1 on October 17, followed a 2-0 win over NYCFC on October 14, and before that hammered DC 4-0 on October 10. Another win would extend that run to four games and keep them rolling into the next stretch of the season.
Red Bulls projected lineup
Michael Bradley sends out a 4-3-3 with Ethan Horvath behind a back line of Dylan Nealis, Jahkeele Marshall-Rutty, Julian Bazan and Devin Padelford. Ronald Donkor, Adri Mehmeti and Mohammed Sofo make up the midfield, with Cameron Harper, Cade Cowell and Julian Hall forming the front line. There are no absences to factor in, so Bradley has his full group available to try to snap the team’s two-game losing run.
Red Bulls projected starting XI (4-3-3): Ethan Horvath, Dylan Nealis, Jahkeele Marshall-Rutty, Julian Bazan, Devin Padelford, Ronald Donkor, Adri Mehmeti, Mohammed Sofo, Cameron Harper, Cade Cowell, Julian Hall. Coach: Michael Bradley.
Inter Miami projected lineup
Kily Gonzalez lines Inter Miami up in a 4-3-3 built around the spine of Casemiro, Rodrigo De Paul and David Ayala in midfield, protecting a back four of Gonzalo Lujan, Micael and Sergio Reguilon. Lionel Messi, Luis Suarez and German Berterame lead the attack, with Matias Galarza completing the midfield unit and Dayne St. Clair in goal. With no absences reported, Gonzalez can field his strongest available group as Inter Miami look to extend their three-game winning streak.
Inter Miami projected starting XI (4-3-3): Dayne St. Clair, Gonzalo Lujan, Casemiro, Micael, Sergio Reguilon, Rodrigo De Paul, David Ayala, Matias Galarza, Lionel Messi, Luis Suarez, German Berterame. Coach: Kily Gonzalez.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo is on the verge of matching his Manchester United goal total at Al Nassr
items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo is on the verge of matching his Manchester United goal total at Al Nassr, with a disputed strike against Al Faisaly putting him closer than ever. 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s career has been defined by milestones, and one more is within reach at Al Nassr. The Portuguese star is closing in on a number that would link two very different chapters of his career: the goals he scored in the Premier League era at Manchester United and his production in Saudi Arabia.



With his latest strike against Al Faisaly, which the Saudi Pro League credited to him in Al Nassr’s 3-1 win, Ronaldo reached 135 goals for Al Nassr in all competitions. At Manchester United, he scored 145 across his two spells, 118 in the first and 27 in the second, leaving him 10 goals shy of matching that tally.



The count comes with a caveat, as several data providers recorded the goal against Al Faisaly as an own goal by defender Andrei Girotto. However, the Saudi Pro League credited the strike to the Portuguese star, which takes his official career tally to 982 goals.



Most of his goals for Al Nassr have come in the Saudi Pro League, where he has scored 107, and he has also found the net in the AFC Champions League, the Arab Club Champions Cup and domestic cups.




Years from now, we’ll look at this and say: we were there for it 💛 pic.twitter.com/W2JIHjp3lG— AlNassr FC (@AlNassrFC_EN) October 23, 2026




Ronaldo’s scoring rate has doubled since leaving Manchester United



The comparison shows how Ronaldo’s scoring rate has changed. Over two spells at Manchester United, he scored 145 goals in 346 appearances, an average of 0.42 goals per game. 


        


At Al Nassr, entering the match against Al Faisaly, he had 134 goals in 159 appearances, roughly double the rate at 0.84 goals per game, while scoring one every 103 minutes compared with one every 183 at United.



Manchester UnitedAl NassrAppearances346159Goals145134Assists5723Goals per game0.420.84Minutes per goal183103Hat-tricks36



Ronaldo has also scored more often from the penalty spot in Saudi Arabia, with 32 of his goals coming from penalties compared with 21 at United, and he has scored 17 headers for Al Nassr compared with 24 for the English club.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo on verge of breaking all-time heading record as Saudi Pro League recognizes his 982nd career goal: How many more does he need?
items.description:
The Portuguese superstar continues to chase historic milestones, and his latest achievement has brought renewed attention to a record that has stood for generations. 
Cristiano Ronaldo has added another chapter to his remarkable goalscoring career after Al Nassr’s latest Saudi Pro League victory sparked debate over his official tally. The Portuguese superstar continues to chase historic milestones, and his latest achievement has brought renewed attention to a record that has stood for generations.



His goal against Al-Faisaly was also at the center of a dispute between the Saudi league’s official records and international statistics providers. While the controversy raised questions about how goals are credited, the decision has kept Ronaldo’s pursuit of soccer history firmly in the spotlight.



Al-Nassr defeated Al Faisaly 3-1 away from home, with Ronaldo scoring in the 49th minute after connecting with a free-kick delivery from fellow Portuguese international Joao Felix. Abdullah Al-Hamdan had opened the scoring earlier, while Theo Bongonda reduced the deficit before Ângelo Gabriel secured the victory.



Ronaldo appeared to score again shortly after his first goal, but his second effort was ruled out following a VAR review. When asked about the situation, the forward reportedly responded humorously: “Only one counted.” The debate continued because several international statistics platforms reportedly attributed the 49th-minute strike to an own goal by rival defender Andrei Girotto.



Cristiano Ronaldo when asked if he scored two goals.He replied:"Only one counted."😄 pic.twitter.com/c3G7w73j3b— The Nassr Tribune™️ (@AlNassrTribune) October 23, 2026 



However, the match referee, Abdullah Al Owaidan, credited Ronaldo with the goal in his official report, a decision reflected in the Saudi Pro League’s records. Saudi media have confirmed that the final decision on goal attribution rests with the Referees Committee of the Saudi Arabian Football Federation. The league relies on the referee’s official report rather than automatically adopting the figures published by independent statistics providers.



CRISTIANO RONALDO'S 982ND CAREER GOAL.🐐There's no doubt about it. pic.twitter.com/NgM576NekB— The Nassr Tribune™️ (@AlNassrTribune) October 24, 2026 



Ronaldo’s latest goal takes him to 982 career strikes



With the Saudi Pro League recognizing the goal, Ronaldo’s official career tally stands at 982 goals for club and country. The achievement moves the Al Nassr forward closer to another landmark as he continues his pursuit of 1,000 career goals.



The discrepancy highlights how different organizations can record the same incident differently. Although independent data providers may maintain their own assessments, the Saudi competition has backed the referee’s attribution in this case.



For Ronaldo, the distinction matters because every officially credited goal contributes to his personal record. His latest strike therefore carries significance beyond Al Nassr’s three points, adding another milestone to a career already filled with individual achievements.



Cristiano Ronaldo of team Al Nassr after winning against Abha



How close is Ronaldo to Jimmy McGrory’s headed-goal record?



Ronaldo’s latest header has also brought attention to a separate historical achievement: the record for the most headed goals in soccer history. According to Wikipedia‘s historical compilation, citing the International Football Association Board (IFAB)‘s metrics, Celtic legend Jimmy McGrory leads the list with 162 headed goals, while Ronaldo has reached 159.



That leaves the Portuguese forward three headed goals short of McGrory’s reported total, following his strike against Al Faisaly. Based on the cited tally, Ronaldo needs three more headed goals to equal McGrory’s 162 and four to surpass him outright.



RankPlayerNationCareer SpanHeaded Goals1.Jimmy McGroryScotland1921–19371622.Cristiano RonaldoPortugal2002–Present1593.Fred RobertsNorthern Ireland1922–19381424.Mario JardelBrazil1991–20111325.SantillanaSpain1970–19881296.Jared BorgettiMexico1994–20101277.Dixie DeanEngland1923–19401258.Telmo ZarraSpain1939–1957122



McGrory established his reputation as a prolific goalscorer during his Celtic career between 1921 and 1937. However, historical goal records from that era are difficult to standardize because complete match records and consistent statistical methods were not always available.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo offers cheeky response amid confusion over his latest 982nd career goal
items.description:
As Al-Nassr secured a triumphant conquest, Cristiano Ronaldo's joyous celebration of his 982nd career strike was quickly met with whispers of doubt. 
The eternal quest for 1,000 goals has encountered a storm of controversy under the desert lights. As Al-Nassr secured a triumphant conquest, Cristiano Ronaldo‘s joyous celebration of his 982nd career strike was quickly met with whispers of doubt. A fateful deflection off a defender’s challenge ignited a fierce debate over the true author of the goal, forcing the Saudi Pro League to intervene.



Al-Nassr claimed a 3-1 win over Al-Faisaly at Al Majma’ah Sports City Stadium, strengthening its position in the Saudi Pro League standings. Abdullah Al-Hamdan opened the scoring in the fourth minute before Ronaldo doubled the advantage shortly after half-time.



Al-Faisaly responded through Theo Bongonda in the 66th minute, but Ângelo Gabriel restored Al-Nassr’s two-goal cushion with a strike in the 79th minute. Ronaldo also appeared to score again shortly after his first goal, although his effort in the 52nd minute was disallowed following a VAR review, leaving him with one goal officially credited during the match.



The controversy centered on Ronaldo’s 49th-minute strike, which several international statistics providers reportedly recorded as an own goal by Al-Faisaly defender Andrei Girotto. Platforms including Opta, SofaScore, FotMob and Flashscore initially differed from the Saudi league’s reported attribution, creating uncertainty over whether the Portuguese forward would receive credit.



Cristiano Ronaldo goal number 982 ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/4yV8r6iJMY— Roshn Saudi League (@SPL_EN) October 23, 2026 



The distinction matters because Ronaldo’s career tally now stands at 982 goals according to the Saudi Pro League’s official record, leaving him 18 short of the widely anticipated 1,000-goal milestone. With every goal closely tracked by supporters, even a disputed deflection has become significant in the debate surrounding his historic pursuit.



Ronaldo delivers cheeky response



When asked about whether he had scored twice, Ronaldo responded with a short remark that appeared to acknowledge the controversy surrounding the match. “Only one counted,” the forward said, offering a lighthearted response to the confusion over his goals.



Cristiano Ronaldo when asked if he scored two goals.He replied:"Only one counted."😄 pic.twitter.com/c3G7w73j3b— The Nassr Tribune™️ (@AlNassrTribune) October 23, 2026 



The comment reflected the difference between celebrating an apparent second strike and having it officially recognized. Although Ronaldo found the net again during the match, VAR ruled the effort out, meaning it could not be added to his career total.



Why the Saudi league’s decision matters



According to reports shared by Saudi sports journalists, referee Abdullah Al Owaidan credited Ronaldo with Al-Nassr’s second goal in his official match report. The Saudi Pro League reportedly follows the referee’s documentation for goal attribution, with the Referees Committee of the Saudi Arabian Football Federation holding responsibility for reviewing disputed decisions.



SPL’s official confirmation of Ronaldo’s goal



Al-Riyadhiah further explained that the league does not simply adopt goal tallies published by international data providers such as Opta. Instead, the referee’s report serves as the official record, and any discrepancies can be referred to the committee for review and possible correction.



The league’s reported decision therefore supports Ronaldo’s 982-goal tally, even though some independent platforms have classified the strike differently. Whether those providers will eventually amend their records remains unclear.

items.title: Jose Mourinho rejects altering Real Madrid’s identity for Lamine Yamal ahead of Barcelona clash
items.description:
Jose Mourinho says Real Madrid will not change their structure for Lamine Yamal ahead of the Clasico against Barcelona. 
The first Clasico of the season is almost here, and with it comes Jose Mourinho’s return to Camp Nou as Real Madrid manager. Ahead of the match on Sunday, the Portuguese coach faced the press and addressed several of the main storylines surrounding the game, including one of Barcelona’s biggest stars.



Asked about Lamine Yamal, Mourinho made it clear that Real Madrid will not tailor their approach to the young winger. “He’s a great player, and great players are respected,” he said. “One thing is respecting, another is changing plans, changing structures, forgetting your own essence. We won’t do that with him or with any other super-quality opponent we play, not just in this match, but in many matches“.



The former Chelsea and Inter Milan manager kept a conciliatory tone toward his rivals throughout the news conference. He said he could not find a single player who isn’t very good at either Real Madrid or Barcelona, and he praised Hansi Flick, calling the German coach “a great coach” who is “doing an excellent job.”



Barcelona arrive at El Clasico as clear LaLiga leaders, with a perfect record of nine wins from nine matches and 27 points. The defending champions had won their first 11 games across all competitions, a run that ended with a 4-2 defeat at PSG in the Champions League in their latest fixture.




🎙️ Mourinho 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/QcBniIRbHY— Real Madrid C.F. 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@realmadriden) October 24, 2026




Real Madrid, on the other hand, sit third with 21 points after winning seven league games and losing two, and they arrive on the back of 4-1 wins over Sevilla in LaLiga and Leipzig in the Champions League.


        


Kounde and Vinicius ruled out of El Clasico



Barcelona will be without Jules Kounde, who suffered a sprained left ankle in last weekend’s win over Real Betis and also missed the Champions League defeat at PSG. 



The club had hoped to have the French defender back for the Clasico, but Hansi Flick confirmed that it will not happen. “Jules won’t be there tomorrow, we don’t want to risk him, he isn’t arriving at the right moment, but we have to accept it,” the German coach said.



Real Madrid will also have to cope without a key attacker, as Vinicius Junior is serving a four-game ban after his red card against Villarreal for pulling an opponent’s hair. 



The Spanish federation’s disciplinary committee gave him two games for the offense and two more for his protests to the referee. The suspension has already kept him out of the win over Sevilla and will also rule him out of the matches against Racing Santander and Valencia.

items.title: Inter Miami congratulate Lionel Messi after receiving Princess of Asturias Award for Sports
items.description:
Inter Miami joined the wave of tributes for Lionel Messi after the Argentine star was honored with one of Spain’s most prestigious awards, capping a special trip back to the country where he built much of his legend. The MLS club shared a message on X congratulating its captain on the 2026 Princess of Asturias […] 
Inter Miami joined the wave of tributes for Lionel Messi after the Argentine star was honored with one of Spain’s most prestigious awards, capping a special trip back to the country where he built much of his legend.



The MLS club shared a message on X congratulating its captain on the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports. “Congratulations, captain, on receiving the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports. Your talent makes history. Your values leave a mark that goes far beyond soccer,” the post read.



Messi received the distinction from Princess Leonor at the Teatro Campoamor in Oviedo, where he was greeted by a standing ovation. The jury recognized him for being the player with the most titles in soccer history, as well as for his talent, his humility and his charity work promoting education and health care for children. Messi did not give a speech at the ceremony and became the third soccer player to win the award, following Iker Casillas and Xavi Hernandez in 2012.



During her address, the princess described Messi as someone who “turned the extraordinary into routine” while putting the collective game above ego. The 39-year-old will now return to the United States, where Inter Miami visit the New York Red Bulls on Oct. 24, before his attention turns to the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony in London on Oct. 26, where he is among the nominees.




Felicitaciones, capitán, por recibir el Premio Princesa de Asturias de los Deportes 2026. 🩷🔟 Tu talento hace historia. Tus valores dejan una huella que va mucho más allá del fútbol. pic.twitter.com/SYOWbnMEcH— Inter Miami CF (@InterMiamiCF) October 23, 2026




Messi dedicates the award to his late father



Messi did not give a speech at the ceremony, but he spoke with the news agency EFE about what the award meant to him, remembering his father, Jorge Messi, who recently passed away. “My father was extremely excited about this award,” the Inter Miami star said.


        


Messi explained that the trip was complicated by his match schedule, but that his father had always insisted he make the journey. “We knew it would be difficult because of my match schedule, but he really insisted that we come, that I travel here to spend these days and receive the award,” he said. “This award goes beyond what you do on the pitch or what I’ve achieved throughout my career. He was very happy about this recognition, and that’s why I’m sure he’s enjoying it too”.



The award adds another honor to a career that has already collected nearly every major distinction in the sport, but this one carried a deeper personal meaning for Messi. 



Keeping his father’s wish in mind, he spent 36 hours in Oviedo and then skipped the post-ceremony cocktail to head straight back to the United States, a reminder that, even on one of the most emotional weeks of his life, soccer remains at the center of everything he does.

items.title: Neymar leaves Lionel Messi’s Barcelona out of the conversation when naming the prime of his career
items.description:
Neymar says his best version came at PSG and not during the MSN era with Lionel Messi at Barcelona, despite winning a treble alongside him. 
Few players have had a career as decorated as Neymar’s, and the MSN trio he formed with Lionel Messi and Luis Suarez at Barcelona marked an era in world soccer. 



The three forwards dominated defenses across Europe and led the club to a historic treble in 2015, winning LaLiga, the Copa del Rey and the Champions League. Even so, Neymar feels his best version did not come during that stage of his career.



The Brazilian made that clear while speaking with Argentine streamer Davoo Xeneize in a video on the creator’s YouTube channel, where he named Paris Saint-Germain as the club where he reached his prime.



“For me, the prime was at Paris Saint-Germain, when I played there. People remember Barcelona because of the MSN (Messi, Suarez, Neymar), but as a player I think PSG was my prime because I had strength, speed and intelligence there, I already knew the whole pitch, and for me that was my best version,” he said.









The answer stands out given Neymar’s four seasons in Catalonia between 2013 and 2017, before his move to PSG that summer. In Paris he won four Ligue 1 titles, and his reasoning has more to do with his maturity as a player, with the physical and tactical knowledge he had gained, than with trophies.


        


Barcelona vs PSG: how Neymar’s two eras compare



The statistics help explain Neymar’s view. With Barcelona, he scored 105 goals in 186 official matches, with 2014-15 standing out as his best campaign, when he netted 39 times in 51 games. In Paris, he scored 118 goals in 173 matches, a better goals-per-game rate than in Spain, and became the club’s fourth all-time top scorer.



The trophy cabinets tell a different story. Neymar won ten major trophies at Barcelona, including two LaLiga titles, three Copa del Rey trophies and the Champions League, all of them alongside Messi. At PSG he collected 13 domestic trophies, led by five Ligue 1 crowns, but never won a European title.



BarcelonaPSGSeasons4 (2013-17)6 (2017-23)Matches186173Goals105118Goals per match0.560.68Champions League titles10League titles25



Whether his prime came in Catalonia or in Paris, Neymar’s career leaves little doubt about his talent, and the debate over which era was his best is likely to continue among fans. Now back at Santos, the club where it all began, the Brazilian can at least say he has chosen his own answer.

items.title: Lamine Yamal, Kylian Mbappe, and Erling Haaland warned as Robert Lewandowski delivers harsh reality check to young stars with stark prediction about their futures
items.description:
Robert Lewandowski has offered a sobering assessment of the challenges awaiting these superstars, questioning whether they can sustain their dominance for as long as the legends who came before them. 
Lamine Yamal, Kylian Mbappe, and Erling Haaland are among the leading figures of soccer’s next generation, with their extraordinary talent and early achievements raising expectations about what they could accomplish. However, Robert Lewandowski has offered a sobering assessment of the challenges awaiting these superstars, questioning whether they can sustain their dominance for as long as the legends who came before them.



Yamal has emerged as one of Barcelona’s most exciting young players, achieving milestones at an age when many players are still developing in academy systems. His rapid rise has naturally prompted comparisons with Lionel Messi, who spent years establishing himself before becoming one of the most dominant players in soccer history.



Mbappe and Haaland have followed similarly remarkable paths, becoming prolific goalscorers and central figures for their respective clubs while still relatively young. Their achievements suggest they have the talent to define the next era, but it raises a different question: how long can they maintain their current standards?



The modern soccer calendar places enormous demands on elite players through domestic leagues, continental competitions, international fixtures, and expanded tournaments. Reaching the top early can mean facing years of physical and mental pressure before many previous generations had even reached their peak.



Kylian Mbappe, Lamine Yamal and Erling Haaland.



Lewandowski questions the longevity of soccer’s next generation



Lewandowski shared his perspective in an interview with The Athletic’s Paul Tenorio, reflecting on the differences between his generation and the teenagers already competing at the highest level. The Polish striker believes modern players reach elite status much earlier, creating challenges that may become more apparent as their careers progress. “For the future it will be impossible to stay on the top for the long term, as we did or we are doing,” Lewandowski said. 



He explained that young players now have access to opportunities and rewards much earlier than previous generations, leaving them with less time to develop gradually. “Our generation, to get something, we needed more time, we need to be more patient,” he added. “Now it’s too fast for the young player… they’re starting much earlier.”



Robert Lewandowski #9 speaks to the media during a press conference.



The stark prediction behind Lewandowski’s warning



The Chicago Fire forward believes the rapid rise of young talents could eventually affect their motivation to remain at the summit of the sport. His prediction is that players who achieve success too easily and too early may eventually lose the hunger required to stay at the top.



“Even though they are amazing players, they reach faster the highest level than our generation did, but probably because of this also it will be more tough for them staying on the top level,” the 38-year-old striker explained.



He also stressed that the challenge extends beyond mentality, pointing to the physical demands of a long career at the highest level. “It’s not easy to play on the top level so many years,” he said, suggesting that the combination of early success and accumulated fatigue could make sustained excellence increasingly difficult.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s Al Nassr suffer blow ahead of Al Kholood clash as Samu Costa must serve one-game ban
items.description:
Al Nassr will be without midfielder Samu Costa for their next Saudi Pro League match against Al Kholood after he accumulated four yellow cards. 
Cristiano Ronaldo led Al Nassr to a 3-1 victory over Al Faisaly, scoring the team’s second goal to extend his career tally to 982. Despite the win, the Saudi side suffered a setback that will be felt in their next Saudi Pro League match.



Ange Postecoglou’s side will be without midfielder Samu Costa for the league clash against Al Kholood, as the Portuguese player has been suspended for accumulating yellow cards.



Costa picked up his fourth booking of the season in the win over Al Faisaly, which triggers an automatic one-match ban. His previous yellow cards came in the league games against Al Ittihad, Al Khaleej and Neom.



The midfielder has been a regular presence in the team this season, making nine league appearances, eight of them as a starter, and scoring three goals. He was left out of the squad for the trip to Al Riyadh in August for squad management reasons.



Samu Costa of Al Nassr. (Getty Images)



Who could replace Costa in Al Nassr’s midfield?



Costa has formed a midfield partnership with Abdullah Al-Khaibari in recent matches, so Ange Postecoglou will have to find a new partner for the Al Kholood clash. One option is Angelo, who started alongside the pair in the 1-0 win over Neom and came off the bench against Al Faisaly.


        


The Brazilian would give the team a more attacking profile, as he usually operates from midfield toward the opposing goal. Playing him in Costa’s place would add more creativity and forward movement, though it could come at the cost of some of the balance Costa provides.



If Postecoglou prefers to keep a similar profile to Costa’s, he could instead turn to Sami Al-Najei and Hayder Abdulkareem, two midfielders who were among the substitutes against Al Faisaly. Costa will remain available for Al Nassr’s AFC Champions League Elite match against Al-Wasl on Oct. 26, as his ban only covers the next league fixture.

items.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
items.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken clubThe big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo scores against 163rd different club as Al-Faisaly joins his record-breaking list: How does Lionel Messi’s total compare?
items.description:
While the 41-year-old remains focused on reaching 1,000 goals, his latest achievement has added another chapter to his long-running statistical rivalry with Lionel Messi. 
Cristiano Ronaldo continues his pursuit of soccer history as Al-Nassr faced Al-Faisaly in the Saudi Pro League, with the Portuguese forward closing in on another remarkable career milestone. While the 41-year-old remains focused on reaching 1,000 goals, his latest achievement has added another chapter to his long-running statistical rivalry with Lionel Messi.



Al-Nassr secured a 3-1 victory over Al-Faisaly, strengthening its position in the Saudi Pro League title race. Abdullah Al-Hamdan opened the scoring in the fourth minute before Ronaldo doubled the advantage with a header in the 49th minute from a João Félix free kick.



The Portuguese captain briefly appeared to have scored again shortly afterwards, but VAR ruled out his second effort for offside. Theo Bongonda pulled one back for Al-Faisaly in the 66th minute, raising hopes of a comeback before substitute Angelo Gabriel sealed the victory with a finish in the 79th.



Ronaldo’s header took his career tally to 982 goals in 1,341 appearances, leaving him 18 short of the unprecedented 1,000-goal feat. The forward had remained on 981 since scoring against Neftchi Fargona on October 12, making his latest strike a significant step towards the landmark.









How many different clubs have Ronaldo and Messi scored against?



Ronaldo’s latest achievement also adds to his record of scoring against 163 different clubs across 49 countries, according to official stats. Al-Faisaly joined that list after the Portuguese star found the net in the Saudi Pro League encounter.



Messi’s total is lower, although the Argentine has also built an extraordinary record across his career with Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain, and Inter Miami. Messi has scored against at least 117 different clubs, as per El Grafico, leaving Ronaldo with a sizeable advantage in the overall number of distinct opponents he has scored against.



Figures can vary depending on the source, the competitions included and how clubs are counted, so the totals should be treated with that context in mind. Messi reached the 100-club milestone with Miami in August 2023, when he scored against Atlanta United in the Leagues Cup, and has continued adding opponents since moving to Major League Soccer.



Lionel Messi of FC Barcelona (L) and Cristiano Ronaldo of Real Madrid CF shake hands



Messi holds his own in Champions League comparison



Although Ronaldo leads in the overall number of different clubs scored against, Messi has been particularly prolific against a wide range of opponents in the UEFA Champions League. The supplied statistics credit Messi with scoring against 40 different teams in the competition, compared with Ronaldo’s 38.



The contrast reflects their different career paths. The Portuguese has played across several domestic leagues, including Portugal, England, Spain, Italy and Saudi Arabia, giving him opportunities to face a wider variety of club opponents.



Messi, meanwhile, spent most of his European career at Barcelona before moving to Paris Saint-Germain and then Inter Miami. His sustained success in Spain and Europe nevertheless helped him build an exceptional record against elite opposition.

items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo moves into the Saudi Pro League top 10 scorers with his fifth goal of the season in Al Nassr’s 3-1 win over Al Faisaly. 
Cristiano Ronaldo returned to the scoresheet for Al Nassr, and the strike moved him into the top 10 of the Saudi Pro League scoring chart. The Portuguese star was on target in a 3-1 win over Al Faisaly that kept the team firmly in the title race.



Ronaldo headed home a Joao Felix free-kick delivery to make it 2-0, his first goal in two matches after failing to score against Neom in his team’s last fixture, when he also missed a penalty. Ronaldo could have added to his total, as a second goal minutes after his header was ruled out for offside following a VAR review.



Although he has now reached five league goals in nine appearances, the 41-year-old remains well adrift of Golden Boot leader Ivan Toney of Al Ahli, who has 11 in eight matches.



Still, the gap is far from insurmountable for a striker with Ronaldo’s pedigree, and a couple of productive outings could quickly bring him back into the conversation at the top of the scoring chart.




Years from now, we’ll look at this and say: we were there for it 💛 pic.twitter.com/W2JIHjp3lG— AlNassr FC (@AlNassrFC_EN) October 23, 2026




The finish took his career tally to 982 goals, leaving him 18 shy of the 1,000 mark, while the win lifts Al Nassr to 25 points. They are now level with league leaders Al Qadsiah, who face third-placed Al Hilal later today in a result that could reshape the title race.


        


Saudi Pro League top 10 scorers



Ronaldo is one of eight players on five goals, with Toney, Youssef En-Nesyri and Mateo Retegui the only players above that mark. This is how the scoring chart looks after Ronaldo’s goal against Al Faisaly:



PlayerTeamGoals1. Ivan ToneyAl Ahli112. Youssef En-NesyriAl Ittihad73. Mateo ReteguiAl Qadsiah64. George IlenikhenaAl Ittihad55. Francisco TrincaoAl Ahli56. Alexandre LacazetteNeom57. Alexandre MendyAl Faisaly58. Steven BergwijnAl Ittihad59. Tijjani ReijndersAl Qadsiah510. Cristiano RonaldoAl Nassr5



With more than two-thirds of the season still ahead, the Golden Boot race is far from decided. Ronaldo and Al Nassr will look to build on this win, as the 41-year-old tries to keep climbing the scoring chart while the team stays in the title hunt.

items.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
items.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now!Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story:“Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.”Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh.Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis.May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee.This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. items.title: Video: Cristiano Ronaldo reaches 982 career goals with latest strike for Al Nassr vs Al Faisaly in Saudi Pro League
items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo scores a header from a Joao Felix free-kick delivery to reach 982 career goals for Al Nassr. 
Cristiano Ronaldo moved closer to one of the most remarkable milestones in football history. The Al Nassr captain scored with a header against Al Faisaly in the Saudi Pro League to reach 982 career goals, leaving him really close from the 1,000 mark.



The goal came from a free kick, which Joao Felix delivered into the box for Ronaldo to head home and extend Al Nassr’s lead to 2-0. It ended a wait for the 41-year-old, who had been stuck on 981 goals since Oct. 12, when he scored in Al Nassr’s 3-1 win over Neftchi Fargona in the AFC Champions League.



Minutes after scoring, the Portuguese forward found the net again to complete a brace, but the goal was reviewed by VAR and ultimately ruled out for offside. Ronaldo now needs 18 more goals to reach 1,000, a milestone that would be unprecedented in the modern game.



JOÃO FÉLIX WITH THE FREE KICK DELIVERY, CRISTIANO RONALDO ASCENDS ABOVE EVERYONE AND THUNDERS A HEADER HOME! 🤯🐐THE MAN IS DEFYING GRAVITY! THE AERIAL DOMINANCE, THE HANG TIME, THE SHEER IMPERIAL AUTHORITY IN THE AIR!FLYING CARS! THE GOAT IS AIRBORNE AGAIN! 🚀💛…— The Nassr Tribune™️ (@AlNassrTribune) October 23, 2026 



Al Nassr stay firmly in the Saudi Pro League title race



With this partial victory, Al Nassr would climb to 25 points if the result holds, level with league leaders Al Qadsiah and one point ahead of third-placed Al Hilal. The leaders would remain first for now on goal difference (+15 to +14), while Al Nassr’s record would stand at eight wins, one draw and one loss.


        


The next result that could reshape the table is a direct clash at the top, as Al Hilal face Al Qadsiah in Matchday 11 today. The challengers have played nine games, one fewer than the two clubs above them, and currently sit on 24 points with the best goal difference in the league (+20).



Al Nassr would be best served by a result that stops Al Hilal from winning. A draw would keep the title race extremely tight, with Al Qadsiah just one point clear and the other two level on 25, while a victory for the leaders would at least keep the team with the game in hand from taking control at the top.



A win for the visitors would be the worst outcome, as it would put them two points clear after entering this round with a match in hand, complicating matters even further for the chasing pack.

items.title: Al-Faisaly vs Al Nassr: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Saudi Pro League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Al-Faisaly vs Al Nassr in the 2026-27 Saudi Pro League. Al-Faisaly host Al Nassr in a Saudi Pro League fixture that pits a team scrapping for points against the two-time champions chasing continued momentum.
Al-Faisaly come into this one off a 2-2 draw with Al Shabab last Sunday, a result that followed a 3-2 win over Al Kholood on October 15. Before that stretch they were beaten 1-3 by Al Ittihad back on September 11, a reminder of the gap that still exists against the league’s top sides. A home result here would settle the nerves after that mixed run and keep Al-Faisaly clear of the bottom of the table.
Al Nassr arrive unbeaten in their last three outings, having edged Neom SC 1-0 on October 20 after a comfortable 3-0 win over Al Diriyah on October 9. They also drew 1-1 with Al Khaleej back on September 12, so the recent form has trended upward since that result. Another win would stretch their momentum further and keep the pressure on the teams above them in the standings.
Al-Faisaly confirmed lineup
Giovanni Solinas sends out a 4-3-3 built around a compact midfield of Andrei Girotto, Jaime Seoane and Abdulaziz Al Bishi, with Flavio and Mohammed Al Shanqiti supplying width from the full-back areas. Abdoulaye Seck and Yaseen Barnawi anchor the back line in front of Fernando Pacheco, while Alexandre Mendy and Abdullah Al-Mogren are tasked with stretching the Al Nassr defense alongside the central midfield trio. With no absences listed, Solinas can field his preferred XI and lean on the side’s organization to try to disrupt Al Nassr’s attacking rhythm.
Al-Faisaly confirmed starting XI (3-4-3): Fernando Pacheco, Yaseen Barnawi, Mohammed Al Shanqiti, Mohammed Jahfali, Abdoulaye Seck, Andrei Girotto, Flávio, Eid Al Muwallad, Alexandre Mendy, Abdulaziz Al Bishi, Abdullah Al Mogren. Coach: Giovanni Solinas.
Al Nassr confirmed lineup
Ange Postecoglou lines Al Nassr up in a 4-4-2, pairing Cristiano Ronaldo with Joao Felix up front and flanking the midfield with Sadio Mane and Angelo Gabriel for width. Inigo Martinez and Abdulelah Al Amri hold the center of defense in front of Bento Krepski, with Nawaf Al-Boushail and Ayman Yahya pushing on from full-back to support the attack. There are no absences to work around, which means Postecoglou can field a settled, attack-minded unit built to carry the recent winning form into the away fixture.
Al Nassr confirmed starting XI (4-4-2): Bento, Nawaf Bu Washl, Awad Aman, Samú Costa, Abdulelah Al Amri, Iñigo Martínez, João Félix, Abdullah Al Khaibari, Cristiano Ronaldo, Abdullah Al Hamddan, Sadio Mané. Coach: Ange Postecoglou.

items.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
items.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amendsPremier League top scorersAfter seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou, the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal, while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season.
